**Source-defined terminology (not inherited hypotheses):** A ring $A$ is **w-contractible** iff every faithfully flat weakly étale map $A\to B$ admits an $A$-algebra retraction. A **pro-étale covering** of $T$ is a family of weakly étale maps whose images admit finite affine-open refinements covering every affine open of $T$.

Let $T = \Spec(A)$ be an affine scheme. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $A$ is w-contractible, and
\item every pro-\'etale covering of $T$ can be refined by
a Zariski covering of the form $T = \coprod_{i = 1, \ldots, n} U_i$.
\end{enumerate}

reason: For w-contractible A, the finite disjoint union of any standard pro-étale cover splits, inducing a clopen Zariski partition refinement. Conversely a finite clopen refinement of every faithfully flat weakly étale affine cover yields a section of Spec B→Spec A and hence an A-algebra retraction.

**Source-defined terminology (not inherited hypotheses):** A ring $A$ is **w-contractible** iff every faithfully flat weakly étale map $A\to B$ admits an $A$-algebra retraction. The small pro-étale site $S_{\proetale}$ uses weakly étale $S$-schemes from a chosen big pro-étale universe; $(\mathrm{Sch}/S)_{\proetale}$ is its big slice site.

Let $S$ be a scheme. The pro-\'etale sites
$S_\proetale$, $(\Sch/S)_\proetale$, $S_{affine, \proetale}$, and
$(\textit{Aff}/S)_\proetale$ and if $S$ is affine $S_{app}$
have enough (affine) quasi-compact, weakly contractible
objects, see Sites, Definition \ref{sites-definition-w-contractible}.
conclusions:
Let $S$ be a scheme. The pro-\'etale sites
$S_\proetale$, $(\Sch/S)_\proetale$, $S_{affine, \proetale}$, and
$(\textit{Aff}/S)_\proetale$ and if $S$ is affine $S_{app}$
have enough (affine) quasi-compact, weakly contractible
objects, see Sites, Definition \ref{sites-definition-w-contractible}.

reason: The assertion is directly reduced to the preceding lemma producing w-contractible affine covers in the big site; its restriction to the listed small and affine sites gives enough weakly contractible objects.
